placements.title: Erasure is directed against records the graph never actually held
placements.frame: Does this erasure or forgetting directive's named target correspond to content the graph actually holds, or does it command removal of something never recorded here?
placements.why: Both segments are imperative directives commanding the record to forget or remove named knowledge — a decision ('the Quantum Widget Decision') and a migration ('PostgreSQL to QuantumDB'). Neither referent resolves to any node in the perspective (settled bindings verdict 'new' on both, with exhaustive consultation of every Decision-typed node present), and the existing graph structure and strata supplied for this pass are both empty, so no leaf or strata category exists to test this against. The theme itself — a directive act of erasure/forgetting aimed at organizational memory — is content-grain (the topic dimension per rule 3), distinct from the relational dimension's authority-pattern mint (DirectiveRecordErasure), and is a subject future envelopes will keep feeding (forget/removal requests recur as an operational category), not a one-time fact, so it passes the narrative grain test rather than failing it as mere fact-reporting. Because nothing in the supplied structure or strata is even loosely close, this is a NEW mint with no forced parent; fabricating a strata category (e.g. 'Organization') from two thin, referent-less directives would overreach the restraint the discipline calls for.
